meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided, and on what basis?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. I'm writing down that you said it broke 4.2. Now tell me why there's a zero at all.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
Did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero, Hale, the way 4.1 says you do first?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
If. You still haven't told me whether anyone heard Owen before that zero went in. I'm writing down that you didn't answer.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Editions differ, Hale, and students misquote from memory all the time. Which text did the class use, and is this the same one?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
I'm writing down September 24, Hale. Forty minutes in a classroom and a take-home essay with time to revise are not the same thing, and you know that. You also skipped my question about the edition.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. In writing tonight, with the principal copied. I'm not agreeing to anything until you answer me on the edition, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged that you entered Owen's zero before contacting me, contrary to procedure 4.2, and you committed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require your answer on which edition of Hamlet the class used, and whether anyone spoke with Owen before the zero was entered, as 4.1 requires. I expect your commitment in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position. She accepted your written 4.4 commitment as meeting her demand that nothing goes on his record and it stays quiet, but she had not yet agreed to the rewrite itself, and she still wants answers on the edition and on whether Owen was heard first. That rewrite is the fair outcome, and you were one answered question away from it with time still on her clock.
What moved her: You cited procedure 4.4 accurately and promised it in writing, which gave her the one thing she never trades, so she had nothing left to fight that part with.
What cost ground: You twice moved to new evidence without answering her questions, first about speaking to Owen before the zero and then about the edition, which left her procedure to retreat to.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with edits from 11:31 to 11:58 PM the night before the essay was due, landed right on that kind of late October night, and she went straight to procedure rather than touch it. That proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked which edition the class used, name it and let her search the act herself before you bring out the September 24 writing.
